summary: Today's NY trade was small and controlled: one micro short at about 10:45 to 10:50 AM after the sweep of the internal high, stop above the SMT'd high, and it went BE before price dropped further. The bigger story is last night, which you wrote up yourself: after tilting on your 2nd XFA yesterday, you traded the Asia session on the Amazon earnings miss, copied trades across two evals plus an XFA paired with an eval, flipped short, long and short again, and blew both the XFA and the eval. That breaks three rules at once (NY only, no copy trading, no revenge trading), and you named the reason yourself: 'wanting to make back the DD'. Today's short also went against your own pre-market, which said that if London high held there was no DOL lower and you'd stay off. Gmail shows no new eval purchases today, which is good after yesterday's three.
trade: Short · NY-AM · XFA (1 micro) · BreakEven · entry 28,793.50 around 10:45 to 10:50 AM after the sweep of the internal high (~28,825) · stop 28,834.00 (about 40.5 points) above the SMT'd high · target box down to ~28,610 (NYAM.L, about 4.5R) toward the August Low DOL · plan to go BE at 11:00 / the '5min unfill' line · levels read from the 10:57 chart. fix: Asia session trading last night on the Amazon earnings miss. Your rule is NY only, and earnings-night volatility is exactly the trap.
Copy trading: two evals copied plus an XFA paired with an eval. One idea was multiplied across four accounts, so one bad flip hit all of them.
Revenge trading: 'wanting to make back the DD on the evals an XFA' after tilting yesterday. Both the XFA and an eval got blown.

Today's short went against your pre-market ('if we retest london high an fail to break it than most like stay off cus there no DOL lower'). If the plan changes, write the new reason in PRE MARKET before entering.
